notes:
## C# scripting
- **New script** asks **C# or JavaScript**. C# scripts are Unity-style MonoBehaviours (Start, Update, OnTriggerEnter, coroutines, async/await, LINQ, generics and more), compiled to JavaScript so they run in every player: web, Android, Windows, Xbox and the C++ player.
- Familiar Unity types: GameObject, Transform, Rigidbody, Collider, Camera, AudioSource, Animator, Input, Time, Mathf, Physics, PlayerPrefs, JsonUtility, List and Dictionary.
- Public fields show in the Inspector, .cs files can be imported, and the code editor checks C# and jumps to errors. Claude's write_script takes C# too.
- Triggers now fire for kinematic bodies.

## Audio
- Mixer groups and an **Audio Mixer** window, 3D sound (min/max distance, rolloff), pitch and random pitch, fade in, music crossfades, and Audio.play/playMusic/setVolume/mute for scripts.
- Waveform previews in Assets; FLAC, AAC, Opus and WebM import.
- The C++ player gets real 3D panning and an analyser that match the browser.

## C++ player
- **Build for Android → Player: C++ (experimental)**: a small native Android app (OpenGL ES 3) with ads, sign-in, keyboard, gamepads and touch. Its JavaScript engine has no JIT, so busy games can run slower than the WebView player. Keep using the WebView player for store releases for now.
- Pages in the C++ player (Windows and Android) match the browser more closely: inline styles can be changed from scripts, flex and grid items keep their content size, backgrounds reach under see-through borders, page styles beat the built-in defaults, and placeholder text is grey.
- Scene games get the joystick and A/B touch buttons drawn natively.

## Also
- The Android emulator allows slow installs (up to 6 minutes) and says when adb timed out.
- This update is for Windows. The Linux and macOS versions stay on 2.21.0 for now.
